findings.title: New abstract getShortcut() breaks existing OAuth2 grant factories
findings.body: OAuth2GrantTypeFactory previously had no abstract methods, so existing custom grant factories implement only the old methods. Adding abstract getShortcut() means such factories fail to compile when rebuilt, and already-deployed binaries throw AbstractMethodError when DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit iterates all OAuth2GrantType factories and calls getShortcut(). This can break server startup/token issuance for deployments with custom grants. Provide a default method (for example returning the unknown shortcut) instead of an abstract method, or otherwise handle factories that do not supply a shortcut.

findings.title: OAuth2GrantType.Context copy constructor was removed
findings.body: The public Context(Context) copy constructor was removed while Context is the object passed to custom OAuth2GrantType implementations. Code that wrapped or copied a grant context (for example to adjust form parameters before delegating) will no longer compile, and deployed code using the constructor will fail with NoSuchMethodError. Restore the copy constructor and make it copy the newly added grantType field, rather than deleting it.

findings.title: Token issuance now fails for an unregistered grant type instead of using unknown encoding
findings.body: getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext substitutes UNKNOWN only when the GRANT_TYPE attribute is null. If the attribute contains any non-null grant string that is not found in the factory shortcut maps, encodeTokenId throws IllegalStateException. Since TokenManager.initToken now calls this for every access token, previously working flows/custom grants whose grant string is not identical to a registered OAuth2GrantType factory id will fail token creation with a server error instead of issuing a token. Fall back to the UNKNOWN/'na' shortcut for unmapped grant types (and log it) rather than failing issuance.

findings.title: isAccessTokenId matcher has inverted logic and wrong substring offsets
findings.body: Encoded token ids are 2 chars session type + 2 chars token type + 2 chars grant type, so the grant shortcut is substring(4, 6). The matcher uses substring(3, 5) and returns false when that substring equals the expected shortcut (if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false). It therefore does not verify the grant type at all for normal ids and can reject only by coincidence. Events asserting CODE_TO_TOKEN/REFRESH/DEVICE/CIBA token ids will pass even if the wrong grant was encoded. Change to reject when !items[0].substring(4, 6).equals(expectedGrantShortcut).

findings.title: Constructor checks grantType twice and never checks rawTokenId
findings.body: The constructor has Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed") on line 73 instead of requireNonNull(rawTokenId, ...). A null rawTokenId is therefore accepted and later encoded as the literal string "null" after the colon by DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.encodeTokenId, producing a corrupt token id rather than failing fast at construction. Fix the argument to rawTokenId.
